newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close lower despite NCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close lower despite NCD issue.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Friday amid loose liquidity despite the central bank's afternoon issue of T$3 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit, dealers said.

The banking system's daily reserve excess was a positive T$20.7 billion on Thursday, showing abundant liquidity. Dealers said liquidity was expected to remain ample next week as T$24 billion worth of NCDs will mature then to fuel the market.
The overnight interbank rate on Friday ended at 5.569 percent against Thursday's 5.735 close, only slightly outside the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent.
Thirty-day commercial paper ended Friday trading at 5.45-5.50 percent against 5.60-5.75.
The government bond yields continued to fall on Friday on persistent buying that partly reflected investors's shifting to bond buying from a consolidating stock market.
After recent weak performance, the stock index edged up 6.84 points or 0.09 percent to close at 8,004.49, having failed to sustain early-session gains.
The benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield ended at 5.835 percent against Thursday's 5.850 close.
